newsitem.title: GERMANY: German construction investment seen falling.
newsitem.headline: German construction investment seen falling.

text.p: The German construction industry expects building investment in 1997 to fall a real 1.4 percent in west Germany and four to five percent in east Germany, resulting in more job losses, an industry group said on Monday.
The Hauptverband der Deutschen Bauindustrie said it sees no turnaround in construction output before 1998.
Construction investment shrank three percent in the west and 1.7 percent in the east in 1996.

"The decline in construction output will be accompanied by a loss of jobs," the association said in a report. About 60,000 construction sector jobs will be cut in 1997, following a loss of 100,000 jobs last year, it said.
Demand for offices and other commercial buildings is seen declining 2.4 percent overall, dropping one percent in west Germany and five percent in east Germany, it said.
Housing investment should decline 1.7 percent in 1997 after being roughly flat last year, it said.
Public-sector construction fell sharply in 1996 due to budget-cutting efforts, with orders dropping 9.7 percent and output falling 6.8 percent from the year before.
